subject: Problems running blavaan model with equality constraints in Stan

messages.author: ade7e6cb60aa84f9
messages.subject: Problems running blavaan model with equality constraints in Stan
parts:
Hi everyone,
I ran into some problems estimating models that contained equality constraints. Either the Sampler did not start or it completely ignored the equality constraints. This is the model syntax:

Maintenance =~ NA*Pc_Color_NoUp + b1*Pc_Color_NoUp + b2*Pc_Letter_NoUp + b3*Pc_Number_NoUp + b4*Pc_Color_Upd + b5*Pc_Letter_Upd + b6*Pc_Number_Upd
Maintenance ~~ 1*Maintenance

Updating =~  NA*Pc_Color_Upd + b7*Pc_Color_Upd + b8*Pc_Letter_Upd + b9*Pc_Number_Upd
Updating ~~ 1*Updating

# Residual covariances for same material
Pc_Color_NoUp ~~ NA*Pc_Color_Upd
Pc_Letter_NoUp ~~ NA*Pc_Letter_Upd
Pc_Number_NoUp ~~ NA*Pc_Number_Upd

# Constrain error variances
Pc_Color_NoUp  ~~ e1*Pc_Color_NoUp
Pc_Letter_NoUp ~~ e2*Pc_Letter_NoUp
Pc_Number_NoUp ~~ e3*Pc_Number_NoUp

Pc_Color_Upd   ~~ e4*Pc_Color_Upd
Pc_Letter_Upd  ~~ e5*Pc_Letter_Upd
Pc_Number_Upd  ~~ e6*Pc_Number_Upd

# equality constraints
b5 == (b4/b7) * b8
b6 == (b4/b7) * b9

I ensured that only one variable is on the left hand side of the equation. But Stan still does not start to sample or ignores the equality contraint (Slack > 50). Are there any other options to specify equality constraints? Or do I miss some error in the specification. In lavaan the model runs as I would expect and meets the equality constraints.
Thanks in advance for any suggestions or comments.
Best, Gidon

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Problems running blavaan model with equality constraints in Stan
parts:
Gidon,

Assuming you are using target="stan", you could instead try one of the other targets (stanclassic, stancond, jags). This type of constraint does not work with target="stan" because the Stan model is pre-compiled there, and it is tough to hard-code every equality constraint that a user might request. But I would have hoped that blavan produced an error message related to that; I will have to look into that.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Problems running blavaan model with equality constraints in Stan
parts:
Hi Ed,
thank you for the quick response. Indeed, I ran the models with the target = "stan" option. However, if I run the models using the option "stanclassic", then I get a warning that I need to "include a target += statement with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform". The mode compiles and samples, however the chains do not converge and the results are not really reasonable. With the "stancond" option I do not get a warning, but the chains still do not converge and the results similarly do not seem reasonable to me.
But running the models in "jags" seems to work. There, I get results (i.e. parameter estimates) that are comparable with the frequentist estimates, which makes sense to me.
Thank you for your efforts!
Best, Gidon

parts: Thanks for the updates, and see below...

On Fri, 2021-01-29 at 07:15 -0800, 'Gidon Frischkorn-Bartsch' via blavaan wrote:
Hi Ed,
thank you for the quick response. Indeed, I ran the models with the target = "stan" option. However, if I run the models using the option "stanclassic", then I get a warning that I need to "include a target += statement with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform".
I think that is because blavaan is using a custom-defined likelihood there, and Stan can't tell whether something sketchy is happening. But I believe it is working as intended.

The mode compiles and samples, however the chains do not converge and the results are not really reasonable. With the "stancond" option I do not get a warning, but the chains still do not converge and the results similarly do not seem reasonable to me.
But running the models in "jags" seems to work. There, I get results (i.e. parameter estimates) that are comparable with the frequentist estimates, which makes sense to me.

Looking at your model again, I wonder whether you are including the argument std.lv=TRUE? It looks like you are fixing lv variances to 1 manually, but blavaan needs to do some extra stuff behind the scenes to make sure those models converge. Those extra things are triggered by std.lv=TRUE.

If that doesn't help, I have observed that Stan can sometimes be more sensitive to priors, as compared to jags. If you are using the blavaan defaults, you might consider trying priors suited to your data. Here are some details:

http://faculty.missouri.edu/~merklee/blavaan/prior.html

Ed

Thank you for your efforts!
Best, Gidon

When you add the std.lv=T argument, you have to take out the parts of the model syntax that are involved in this constraint. As the syntax will come first and still affect the model
